questions.q: By what other name are the generations of Esau called?
questions.a: The generations of Esau are also called Edom.

questions.q: From where did Esau get his wives?
questions.a: Esau took his wives from the Canaanites.

questions.q: Why did Esau move away from his brother Jacob?
questions.a: Esau moved away from his brother Jacob because the land could not support both of them, for their possessions were too many.
Esau settled in the mountains of Seir.

questions.q: What was the name of the son born by Timna, a concubine of Esau’s firstborn-son Eliphaz?
questions.a: The name of the son born by Timna was Amalek.

questions.q: Who was the father of the inhabitants of the land in which Edom lived?
questions.a: Seir the Horite was the father of the inhabitants of the land in which Edom lived.

questions.q: What did the people of Edom have before Israel had them?
questions.a: The people of Edom had kings before any king reigned over the sons of Israel.

questions.q: Who was the father of the Edomites?
questions.a: Esau was the father of the Edomites.

commentary.text: —The registers in this chapter show the faithfulness of God to his promise to Abraham. Esau is here called Edom, that name which kept up the remembrance of his selling his birth-right for a mess of pottage. Esau continued the same profane despiser of heavenly things. In outward prosperity and honour, the children of the covenant are often behind, and those that are out of the covenant get the start. We may suppose it a trial to the faith of God's Israel, to hear of the pomp and power of the kings of Edom, while they were bond-slaves in Egypt; but those that look for great things from God, must be content to wait for them; God's time is the best time. Mount Seir is called the land of their possession. Canaan was at this time only the land of promise. Seir was in the possession of the Edomites. The children of this world have their all in hand, and nothing in hope, Lu 16:25; while the children of God have their all in hope, and next to nothing in hand. But, all things considered, it is beyond compare better to have Canaan in promise, than mount Seir in possession.
